texts: good. the meeting, its emergency-meeting kind, the Council as the one holding it, and all three time pieces (Year 1, day 17, afternoon) are carried, and the day-index rides the ordinary calendar day slot without loss. One thing to be aware of: the opening date frame lands on the meeting alone, so the later sentences of this episode carry no time of their own.

mixed: the decision and its to-begin complement both come through correctly (the Council is the one who would begin, and nothing falsely claims the additions actually started), but 'immediately' has no slot in the translator's vocabulary and is simply dropped, so the urgency of the decision is lost. Say the timing as a time the translator can carry instead: 'The Council decided to begin salt-bloom additions that afternoon.'

good. Hesper, the pouches, the salt-bloom they hold and the Cliff Path keepers as recipients are all covered. The container link ('pouches of salt-bloom') is recorded on an improvised of-atom rather than a dedicated one, but no content is lost, and rephrasing it as 'salt-bloom pouches' would be worse — it would bury salt-bloom inside a compound name.

bad: the message itself is lost. A that-clause whose content is entirely negative ('needed no salt-bloom') has no way to carry its negation inside the translator's sealed-complement form, so the parse keeps only 'the Council told the keepers of the Northcove' and drops everything that was told. State the content as its own clause: 'The Council spoke to the keepers of the Northcove. The Northcove did not need salt-bloom.' The price is that the passage now commits to the fact rather than only reporting it, but that is the only way to keep the content at all.
good. the recording event, the cold snap with its cold/snap decomposition, the ledger it went into and the past tense are all carried.
